items.title: Brunies Brother Band Interview, 1957-10-19
items.q: I'd call up Emil Christian. He was a trumpet player. I said, Emil, how about playing a half a night for me?

ctx.x: . Now we have some time. Yeah, it's going all right now. If you can just tell us first, forget your name on Abby, so we know. Okay, this is Abby Brunus speaking. And now these folks are here wanting to know how I started. It's been so long, it's hard to remember. We're back there in 1908. When were you born? In 1900. And we started out, I think we were the first school band in the United States. There was only three pieces. And the three pieces consist of Emmett Rogers, George Brunus, and myself. And then we...…

. He played it on the floor like that and stuff. George had people stand on his chest. Yeah, jump on his chest. What we call that eccentric. So Henry did all that too. Henry done that before George did that. Yeah, sure. Henry was really the originator of it. Well, uh, start. I didn't get that on here. You say Henry could read a good reader, but the rest of you never did learn to read. No, none of us read outside of Henry. Henry would sit down and play first chair in a big 60-piece band. items.title: Emile Christian and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-02-11
items.q: I used to play for Merritt sometimes over there.

ctx.x: That's all. I never had no big bands in there. There was only five men over the tracks in the real joint halls over there in the Tangle Palace. I worked there with Henry and Merritt Brunus. And I don't know who played piano. But I'll never forget that place over there. Remember Peg Leg?

Yeah, Anstead. Peggy Anstead. Yeah, an opera. I used to play for Merritt sometimes over there. They had a Jewish fellow piano player. Oh, really? I can't even place what was on. And they had Henry. Henry was playing trombone. I was playing cornet. And I think it was Eagle Beak Lamb that was on drums.
